litematica-printer.config.bedrock.desc: Run an internal bedrock-breaking state machine inside the selection. Requires pistons, redstone torches, slime blocks and a pickaxe that can instant-mine pistons.
litematica-printer.config.breakBlacklist:
Prohibit print-mode auto-breaking from handling blocks in this list.
This mainly affects automatic cleanup of wrong/extra blocks during printing and does not affect mining mode.
Can input item ID or translated name in current language, example: §bminecraft:stone§r §bsandstone§r.
Block state matching is also supported, example: §bminecraft:wheat[age=7]§r.
Prefix §b#§r for tag matching, example: §l#minecraft:logs§r.
Input text and filter conditions simultaneously (separated by English comma), example: §lglazed_terracotta,c§r.
Where "c" represents contains matching, prioritizing pinyin or direct matching.
litematica-printer.config.breakBlocksPer:
Number of blocks mining mode can process per game tick. Higher values mean more blocks mined each time, provided they can be broken within one tick.
Set to §b0§r for no limit.
litematica-printer.config.breakCheckHard: Whether to skip unbreakable blocks (blocks with hardness of -1). If only the hardness of certain blocks has been modified on the server side, you can disable this option.
Automatically switch to a better tool before breaking blocks.
If Tweakeroo's tool switch is enabled, Tweakeroo is used instead to avoid duplicate switching.
Cooldown time after breaking the same position in mining mode (in game ticks). Retry only after the cooldown ends.
litematica-printer.config.bedrockInterva:
Global interval for bedrock execution windows (in game ticks).
After the controller consumes bedrock throughput budget, it waits this many ticks before opening the next execution window.
Set to 0 for continuous execution; higher values are safer but slower.
litematica-printer.config.bedrockBlocksP:
Bedrock throughput limit per game tick.
This directly controls how many targets can advance per tick, how many new targets may be submitted per tick, and how many targets may stay active in parallel.
Higher values are usually faster, but also increase cleanup pressure and machine overlap risk.
litematica-printer.config.bedrockAllowSi:
Allow bedrock breaking to use horizontal piston layouts when no vertical layout is available.
Disabled by default to avoid horizontal look-settle delays slowing multi-layer jobs; when enabled, exposed vertical layouts are still preferred.
litematica-printer.config.bedrockWhiteli:
Additional blocks allowed into the bedrock-breaking state machine.
Can input block ID or translated name in current language, example: §bminecraft:obsidian§r §bobsidian§r.
Prefix §b#§r for tag matching, example: §l#minecraft:dragon_immune§r.
Input text and filter conditions simultaneously (separated by English comma), example: §ldeepslate,c§r.
Where "c" represents contains matching, prioritizing pinyin or direct matching.
litematica-printer.config.bedrockMultipl: Use server RTT and block-update timing to extend confirmation grace and back off retries for the same target. RTT 0 keeps the current singleplayer speed.
litematica-printer.config.mineTrenchMode: Before mining, fill fluids inside the selection and in the blocks immediately beside both sides of a straight selection with sand. Disabled by default.
Interval between mining-mode break actions (in game ticks).
Set to 0 for no interval (may cause server lag), recommended to set to 1-5 to balance speed and performance.
litematica-printer.config.breakLimit.des:
Block filtering rules for print-mode auto-breaking.
§dNo Limit§r: No restriction on print auto-breaking
§dWhitelist§r: Only allow auto-breaking for blocks in the whitelist
§dBlacklist§r: Prohibit auto-breaking for blocks in the blacklist
§lNote:§r This only affects print-mode auto-breaking and does not affect mining mode.§r
litematica-printer.config.breakLimiter.d:
Source of print auto-break rules:
§dTweakeroo Preset§r: Use Tweakeroo mod's break restriction rules
§dCustom§r: Use the printer's custom print auto-break rules.
This only affects print-mode auto-breaking and does not affect mining mode.
litematica-printer.config.breakProgressT:
Finish threshold for continuously mined hard blocks. A STOP packet is sent after this progress is reached.
Mining mode uses a fast START/STOP path for soft blocks with high single-tick break progress and waits for server confirmation, so soft-block speed is usually not controlled by this option.
Higher values are safer; lower values are more aggressive. Keep this higher on servers with stricter break checks.
litematica-printer.config.breakUseDelaye:
Compatibility option for the generic break path.
If a STOP packet is sent before enough progress is reached, the break is moved to the delayed destroy cache.
The new mining executor handles continuous breaking and server confirmation itself, so this is usually not needed for mining mode.
litematica-printer.config.breakWhitelist:
Only allow print-mode auto-breaking to handle blocks in this list.
This mainly affects automatic cleanup of wrong/extra blocks during printing and does not affect mining mode.
Can input item ID or translated name in current language, example: §bminecraft:stone§r §bsandstone§r.
Block state matching is also supported, example: §bminecraft:wheat[age=7]§r.
Prefix §b#§r for tag matching, example: §l#minecraft:logs§r.
Input text and filter conditions simultaneously (separated by English comma), example: §lglazed_terracotta,c§r.
Where "c" represents contains matching, prioritizing pinyin or direct matching.
litematica-printer.config.category.break: Low-level break protocol and progress settings shared by mining and other break flows
litematica-printer.config.category.speci: Toggles for relaxed restrictions, unusual compatibility, and environment-dependent behavior
litematica-printer.config.checkPlayerInt:
When enabled, printer only processes blocks within player's block interaction range.
Positions beyond interaction distance will not perform operations to avoid cross-distance operations being detected by servers.
If you're playing on servers that allow cross-distance interaction, you can disable this option.
litematica-printer.config.closeAllMode.d: Close all working modes; if currently running in single mode, will automatically revert to printing mode.
litematica-printer.config.debugOutput.de:
When enabled, console will output printer debug information.
If §6§lShow Work Status§r is also enabled, some information will also be displayed in the operation interface.
litematica-printer.config.easyPlaceProto:
Use Servex's easy place protocol to handle block placement correction during printing.
§lNote:§r This feature only works in single-player or on servers with Servux installed.
litematica-printer.config.excavateBlackl:
Prohibit mining blocks in this list.
Can input item ID or translated name in current language, example: §bminecraft:stone§r §bsandstone§r.
Block state matching is also supported, example: §bminecraft:wheat[age=7]§r.
Prefix §b#§r for tag matching, example: §l#minecraft:logs§r.
Input text and filter conditions simultaneously (separated by English comma), example: §lglazed_terracotta,c§r.
Where "c" represents contains matching, prioritizing pinyin or direct matching.
Block filtering rules for mining mode.
§dNo Limit§r: No restriction on any block mining
§dWhitelist§r: Only allow mining blocks in whitelist
§dBlacklist§r: Prohibit mining blocks in blacklist
§lNote:§r When using Tweakeroo mining limit presets, this setting will not take effect.§r
litematica-printer.config.excavateLimite:
Source of mining limit rules:
§dTweakeroo Preset§r: Use Tweakeroo mod's mining limit rules
§dCustom§r: Use printer's custom mining limit rules.
litematica-printer.config.excavateWhitel:
Only allow mining blocks in this list.
Can input item ID or translated name in current language, example: §bminecraft:stone§r §bsandstone§r.
Block state matching is also supported, example: §bminecraft:wheat[age=7]§r.
Prefix §b#§r for tag matching, example: §l#minecraft:logs§r.
Input text and filter conditions simultaneously (separated by English comma), example: §lglazed_terracotta,c§r.
Where "c" represents contains matching, prioritizing pinyin or direct matching.
litematica-printer.config.fill.desc: Within the selection range, place blocks configured in §6Fill Block List§r.
Block list used by filling mode, configuration rules consistent with "Basic Block List".
Block selection mode for filling.
§dBlock List§r: Use blocks in configured list
§dHeld Item§r: Use currently held block in main hand
litematica-printer.config.fillModeFacing: Facing settings when filling blocks. For example, placing upper slabs or lower slabs.
litematica-printer.config.fillSelectionT:
Working selection range rules for filling mode:
§dProjection Selection§r: Use complete selection currently selected in projection as working range
§dProjection Render Layer§r: Only execute filling within current render layer range of projection
§dProjection Selection Below Player§r: Only process areas below player's height in selection
§dProjection Selection Above Player§r: Only process areas above player's height in selection
litematica-printer.config.fluid.desc: At lava sources and water sources positions, default place blocks configured in §6Fluid Replacement Block List§r.
litematica-printer.config.fluidList.desc: List of liquids that need to be replaced, can only input liquid IDs, example: §bminecraft:water§r.
litematica-printer.config.fluidModeFillF: When enabled, flowing liquids will also be treated as targets needing filling and replacement.
litematica-printer.config.fluidReplaceBl:
Block list for filling liquids. Can input item ID or displayed name, example: §bminecraft:sand§r §bsand§r.
Prefix §b#§r for tag matching, example: §l#minecraft:sand§r.
litematica-printer.config.fluidSelection:
Working selection range rules for fluid removal mode:
§dProjection Selection§r: Use complete selection currently selected in projection as working range
§dProjection Render Layer§r: Only execute fluid removal within current render layer range of projection
§dProjection Selection Below Player§r: Only process areas below player's height in selection
§dProjection Selection Above Player§r: Only process areas above player's height in selection
litematica-printer.config.mine.desc: Mine all non-liquid blocks within selection range.
litematica-printer.config.mineSelectionT:
Working selection range rules for mining mode:
§dProjection Selection§r: Use complete selection currently selected in projection as working range
§dProjection Render Layer§r: Only execute mining within current render layer range of projection
§dProjection Selection Below Player§r: Only process areas below player's height in selection
§dProjection Selection Above Player§r: Only process areas above player's height in selection (default)
litematica-printer.config.modeSwitch.des:
§dSingle Mode§r: Only run one working mode at a time
§dMulti Mode§r: Can run multiple working modes simultaneously
§lNote:§r Need to reopen settings menu after switching to see mode change effects.§r
litematica-printer.config.multiBreak.des: When enabled, execute operations according to mode priority. Low priority modes will pause when high priority modes are running.
litematica-printer.config.openScreen.des: Hotkey to open printer settings menu (the page you're currently viewing).
litematica-printer.config.placeBlocksPer:
Number of blocks that can be placed per game tick. Higher values mean more blocks placed each time.
Set to §b0§r for no limit.
Cooldown time after placing blocks at the same location (in game ticks). Retry placement operation only after cooldown ends.
§c§lDo not set to 0 unless necessary, otherwise it will cause placing extra blocks, inability to place correctly and other issues!§r
litematica-printer.config.placeRttAdapti:
Automatically raise the placement interval to at least one round-trip (your ping) so a placement is not sent before the server confirms the previous one.
Reduces misplaced/ghost blocks on servers, especially with high latency.
Uses your tab-list ping; has no effect in singleplayer/LAN (ping 0).
litematica-printer.config.placeRttSafety: Use this percentage of the measured RTT as the minimum interval. 100 = exactly one round-trip. Higher is safer but slower; lower is faster but riskier.
litematica-printer.config.placeInAir.des: Ignore block support requirements and place blocks directly in air positions (applicable to unsupported decorative blocks).
litematica-printer.config.printUsePacket:
Print mode only. Skips the vanilla placement flow and local prediction: the UseItemOn packet is sent directly and the block only appears locally once the server confirms it.
Removes ghost blocks caused by local prediction, at the cost of the block appearing one tick later and losing prediction rollback.
Fill/fluid/bedrock are unaffected. Disabled by default; pairs well with 'RTT Adaptive Interval' on servers.
litematica-printer.config.tweakerooAngel: When enabled, players with build permission can also pass Tweakeroo's angel block placement check. This usually affects survival mode.\nWhen disabled, Tweakeroo's original creative-only behavior is preserved.
litematica-printer.config.printSortSides: When enabled, prioritize placement faces that are closer to the player's view and usually easier to click.
litematica-printer.config.printSortTarge: When enabled, prioritize print targets matching the held block, closer to the view direction, and closer to the player.
litematica-printer.config.printRepairRai: When enabled, the printer checks RailShape after placing rails and will break and retry up to 3 times if neighbor updates bend them incorrectly. This is a client-side best-effort repair and cannot fix every vanilla-unstable shape.
Interval time for placing blocks (in game ticks).
May automatically add delays to avoid placement errors for some special blocks.
Setting to 0 may cause poor performance on servers with packet restrictions.
Not recommended to set to 0 when printing redstone mechanisms.
litematica-printer.config.printAutoFillC:
Automatically fill compostable items into composters to generate bone meal.
(§lWarning: This operation will consume compostable items in inventory!§r)

Compostable items used for automatic composter filling.
Can input item ID or translated name in current language, example: §bminecraft:wheat§r §bwheat§r.
Prefix §b#§r for tag matching, example: §l#compostable§r.
Add ",c" after text for contains matching (prioritizing pinyin/direct matching), example: §lwheat,c§r.
litematica-printer.config.printAutoStrip: When enabled, if stripped logs are not in inventory, will first place normal logs, then automatically strip them with axe to save manual operation time.
litematica-printer.config.printAutoTunin: When printing note blocks, automatically tune note blocks to the pitch specified in schematic.
litematica-printer.config.printBreakExtr:
Automatically break extra blocks that don't exist in schematic during printing.
Affected by the print auto-break restriction settings.
litematica-printer.config.printBreakWron:
Automatically break blocks that completely mismatch the schematic during printing.
Affected by the print auto-break restriction settings.
litematica-printer.config.printFallingBl: When enabled, will check if blocks below falling blocks match schematic, and skip placement if incorrect.
litematica-printer.config.printForcedSne: Automatically maintain sneaking state during printing process.
litematica-printer.config.printHotkey.de: When holding the bound hotkey, printer will continuously place blocks.
litematica-printer.config.printIceForWat: Generate water source blocks through "place ice → break ice" method to achieve water source printing.
litematica-printer.config.printMode.repl:
In replacement mode, replace specified source blocks with target blocks in selection area.
Can input source block ID/name and target block ID/name (separated by English colon), example: §bminecraft:stone:minecraft:oak_planks§r §bstone:oak_planks§r.
Prefix §b#§r for tag matching, example: §l#logs:minecraft:oak_planks§r (replace all logs with oak planks).
litematica-printer.config.printReplace.d: Directly overwrite blocks in list without skipping processing or breaking.
litematica-printer.config.printReplaceCo: When printing dead coral, if no dead coral in inventory, use live coral as substitute; if both exist, will prioritize using dead coral.
litematica-printer.config.printReplaceab:
Block list that can be directly overwritten during printing (without breaking original blocks).
Can input item ID or translated name in current language, example: §bminecraft:stone§r §bsandstone§r.
Prefix §b#§r for tag matching, example: §l#minecraft:logs§r.
Add ",c" after text for contains matching, example: §lglazed_terracotta,c§r.
litematica-printer.config.printSafelyObs: Check if suitable for placement before placing observers to avoid accidentally triggering your machines and causing disasters.
litematica-printer.config.printSelection:
Working selection range rules for printing mode:
§dProjection Selection§r: Use complete selection currently selected in projection as working range
§dProjection Render Layer§r: Only execute printing within current render layer range of projection
§dProjection Selection Below Player§r: Only process areas below player's height in selection
§dProjection Selection Above Player§r: Only process areas above player's height in selection (default)
litematica-printer.config.printSkip.desc: When enabled, will skip blocks in the list during printing.
Block list skipped during printing. Can input item ID or translated name in current language, example: §bminecraft:stone§r §bsandstone§r.
Prefix §b#§r for tag matching, example: §l#minecraft:logs§r.
Add ",c" after text for contains matching, example: §lglazed_terracotta,c§r.
litematica-printer.config.printerAutoDis: Automatically disable printer when player dies to avoid misoperations after respawning.
litematica-printer.config.printerIterato:
Area shape for printer block iteration:
§dCube§r: Cube with §6§lWork Radius§r as edge length (recommended value: 3)
§dSphere§r: Sphere with §6§lWork Radius§r as radius (recommended value: 6)
§dOctahedron§r: Octahedron with §6§lWork Radius§r as edge length (recommended value: 6)
litematica-printer.config.printerLagChec: used as the upper limit for lag detection.
litematica-printer.config.printerMode.de:
Printer's core work mode:
§dPrinting§r: Restore blocks in projection blueprint (including direction, state and other properties)
§dMining§r: Mine blocks within selection range (except fluids)
§dBedrock Breaking§r: Break bedrock within selection range using game mechanics (only available for 1.19+ with Bedrock Miner mod installed)
§dFluid Removal§r: Fill liquids in projection selection with specified blocks
§dFilling§r: Fill projection selection with blocks

§lNote:§r Except for §dPrinting§r mode, operation ranges of other modes are all within projection selection, can also be changed by adjusting §6§lSelection Type§r of each mode.
litematica-printer.config.printerSelecti:
Working selection range rules for printing mode:
§dProjection Selection§r: Use complete selection currently selected in projection as working range
§dProjection Render Layer§r: Only execute printing within current render layer range of projection
§dProjection Selection Below Player§r: Only process areas below player's height in selection
§dProjection Selection Above Player§r: Only process areas above player's height in selection
litematica-printer.config.printerWorking:
Number of block operations executed per game tick (only effective when print interval is set to 0).
Recommended to set to 2-8 to balance speed and performance. Too high values may get kicked by server.
litematica-printer.config.quickShulker.d: Directly take needed materials from shulker boxes in inventory for quick item retrieval.
litematica-printer.config.quickShulkerCo: Cooldown time for quick shulker function (in game ticks). Some plugin servers have cooldown restrictions for this function. Set to 0 to disable cooldown.
litematica-printer.config.quickShulkerMo:
§dSimulate Click§r: Right-click shulker box slot in inventory to open (requires server plugin support)
§dInvoke Mod§r: Directly invoke QuickShulker mod to open (requires installation on both sides for normal use)
litematica-printer.config.renderHud.desc:
Display current mode and work progress within range on operation page when printer is working;
If §6§lLag Detection§r is enabled, will show prompt when lag is excessive.
litematica-printer.config.renderHudX.des: Set the X position of the work status HUD.
litematica-printer.config.renderHudY.des: Set the Y position of the work status HUD.
litematica-printer.config.renderHudScale: Set the overall scale percentage of the work status HUD.
litematica-printer.config.renderLayerLim: Limit printer work range to Litematica's currently rendered layer range.
litematica-printer.config.switchPrinterM: Switch the current working mode of the printer (print/mine/bedrock etc).
litematica-printer.config.hudDrag.desc: Hold the key and move the mouse to drag the HUD position; release to save.
litematica-printer.config.unlockBeaconEf:
Relax the client-side beacon UI effect tier limits and allow selecting primary/secondary effects that would normally be unavailable at the current beacon level, similar to wacko-beacons.
This does not change server-side validation; whether it actually works depends on the server still being vulnerable or unpatched.
litematica-printer.config.updateCheck.de: Automatically check for mod updates when first entering world.
litematica-printer.config.scanTimeBudget:
Main-thread time cap for the entry scanner per tick, in milliseconds.
This is a safety fuse, not a performance optimization switch. Raising it only allows more same-tick scanning and may stutter; lowering it yields earlier to the next tick and may refresh targets more slowly.
litematica-printer.config.lazyEnterTicks: Number of continuously idle ticks before the entry scanner enters lazy state; 0 disables lazy scanning.
litematica-printer.config.workRange.desc:
Printer's maximum work radius centered on player (blocks). Larger values mean wider coverage.
This parameter is associated with §6§lIteration Area Shape§r.
litematica-printer.free_notice: Multilingual translation needs improvement, help us please
litematica-printer.message.falling_block: Block %s has no support below, skipping placement
Block %s has mismatched block below, skipping placement
litematica-printer.message.bedrock.creat: Cannot use Bedrock Breaking mode in Creative mode!
litematica-printer.message.inventory.shu: Shulker box is occupying the hotbar
bedrockminer.fail.missing.survival: Bedrock breaking can only be used in survival or adventure mode
bedrockminer.fail.missing.piston: Bedrock breaking failed: not enough pistons in inventory
bedrockminer.fail.missing.redstonetorch: Bedrock breaking failed: missing redstone torch
bedrockminer.fail.missing.slime: Bedrock breaking failed: missing slime block
bedrockminer.fail.missing.instantmine: Bedrock breaking failed: an instant-mining piston setup is required
bedrockminer.fail.place.redstonetorch: Bedrock breaking failed: no valid redstone torch support was found
bedrockminer.fail.place.piston: Bedrock breaking failed: unable to place or restore the piston machine
litematica-printer.update.available: Litematica Printer detected new version! Current version: %s, latest version: %s
litematica-printer.update.download: >> Click here to download latest version <<
litematica-printer.update.failed: Update check failed, please try again later.
litematica-printer.update.recommendation: Strongly recommend upgrading to latest version to fix potential serious issues.
litematica-printer.config.printBonemealC: Use bone meal to grow crops.

How many consecutive bone meal clicks to send each time a crop is processed.
Higher values grow crops faster, but also consume bone meal more aggressively.
litematica-printer.config.breakUsePacket: Send START/STOP destroy packets directly without local prediction; blocks disappear only after server confirmation.
litematica-printer.config.breakSound.des: Play the local break sound when a block is broken; mutes breaking when disabled.
litematica-printer.config.breakVeilToggl: When enabled, blocks in the list are broken instantly with a START+STOP packet pair, ignoring hardness and break progress (the server still has to accept the block as breakable).
Blocks that can be broken instantly. Supports item IDs, translated names, #tags and state matching (e.g. minecraft:wheat[age=7]); @nbt: rules also work.
Collect candidates first, then batch-break them with the same tool (default); when disabled, blocks are broken one by one in scan order.
litematica-printer.config.breakAvoidFlui: Skip breaking blocks adjacent to fluids in the list, protecting dams and floodgates.
litematica-printer.config.breakFluidList: Blocks treated as dangerous fluids; water and lava by default.
litematica-printer.config.breakFluidStra: Five faces: check above/east/west/north/south only; Six faces: also check below the target.
litematica-printer.config.breakAvoidSupp: Skip breaking blocks with a falling block (sand, gravel, anvil, dragon egg) above, preventing cascading collapses.
litematica-printer.config.breakNonBlocki: Pause automatic mining while the player holds the attack key to mine manually.
litematica-printer.config.printSound.des: Play the local placement sound after placing; mutes placement when disabled. In packet mode the sound plays after server confirmation.
litematica-printer.config.printSubstitut: When the required block is missing, place one of the substitutes instead. Format: sub1,sub2:target (e.g. minecraft:deepslate_tiles:minecraft:stone_bricks).
One rule per line: substitutes on the left (comma separated), target on the right (colon separated). Supports item IDs, path names and translated names.
litematica-printer.config.printerIterato: Axis priority when iterating blocks in the work area (default XZY: X fastest, Y slowest).
litematica-printer.config.printerXAxisRe: Iterate the X axis from high to low.
litematica-printer.config.printerYAxisRe: Iterate the Y axis from high to low.
litematica-printer.config.printerZAxisRe: Iterate the Z axis from high to low.
litematica-printer.config.moveAdaptiveIt: In mining mode, extend the work area forward along the dominant movement axis so you dig where you are heading first.
litematica-printer.config.motionAheadBlo: Extra blocks to extend along the dominant movement axis in move-adaptive iteration.
Aim at a container and press the hotkey: every container of the same type inside the Litematica selection gets synced to match its slots. Press again to cancel.
litematica-printer.config.syncInventoryC: Before syncing, check that the player inventory has enough items to reproduce the target container; wait otherwise.
When the target container is a crafter, sync its enabled/disabled slot states too.
litematica-printer.config.syncPacketLimi: Maximum container click packets per game tick during inventory sync, to avoid server kicks.
litematica-printer.config.syncInventoryC: Highlight color for containers being processed by inventory sync.
litematica-printer.config.syncHighlightR: Collection and highlight range for sync target containers (blocks); 0 means unlimited.
litematica-printer.message.inventory_syn: Target block is not a container
Inventory sync in progress, %s containers left
litematica-printer.config.verifierOptimi: Replace the vanilla schematic verifier with an async chunked verifier; faster verification with less stutter on large schematics.
litematica-printer.config.bedrockExterna: Hand bedrock targets to the bedrockminer/blockminer mods (requires one of them); when disabled the built-in bedrock state machine is used.
litematica-printer.config.printScanAutoW: Pathfind and walk to pending targets found by the scan.
Allow aerial pathfinding while riding a happy ghast.
litematica-printer.config.pathNearestTar: Pick the target closest to the player when pathfinding.
litematica-printer.config.goScanExtraBlo: Treat extra blocks as targets during auto-walk scanning.
litematica-printer.config.goScanWrongBlo: Treat wrong blocks as targets during auto-walk scanning.
litematica-printer.config.pathTargetCand: Maximum target candidates per auto-walk scan.
litematica-printer.config.walkScanWhitel: Only auto-walk scan blocks in the whitelist.
Target blocks for auto-walk scanning; supports item IDs, translated names and #tags.
litematica-printer.config.printScanSecti: Axis priority when auto-walk scanning traverses sections.
litematica-printer.config.printScanXReve: Traverse the X axis high to low during auto-walk scanning.
litematica-printer.config.printScanYReve: Traverse the Y axis high to low during auto-walk scanning.
litematica-printer.config.printScanZReve: Traverse the Z axis high to low during auto-walk scanning.
litematica-printer.config.goTimeLimit.de: Time limit for one pathfinding computation (milliseconds).
litematica-printer.config.goMaxFall.desc: Maximum safe fall height for walking pathfinding.
litematica-printer.config.goCostLimitFac: Search cost limit is straight-line distance times this factor; 0 means unlimited.
litematica-printer.config.goHeuristicWei: A* heuristic weight; higher is greedier.
litematica-printer.config.goGhastCostOrt: Cost of orthogonal moves during ghast flight.
litematica-printer.config.goGhastCostDia: Cost of 2D diagonal moves during ghast flight.
Cost of 3D diagonal moves during ghast flight.
litematica-printer.config.goGhastAscendM: Cost multiplier for ascending during ghast flight.
litematica-printer.config.goGhastDescend: Cost multiplier for descending during ghast flight.
litematica-printer.config.goGhastWallPen: Extra cost for flying close to walls.
litematica-printer.config.goGhastVertLat: Weight for deferring vertical movement during ghast flight.
litematica-printer.config.goGhastWaypoin: Timeout for reaching a waypoint during ghast flight (seconds).
litematica-printer.config.goGhastTurnPen: Extra cost for turning during ghast flight.
litematica-printer.config.goWalkCost.des: Base cost of walking one block.

Minimum amount kept for each item.

litematica-printer.config.placeSameItemF: Prefer blocks matching the held item to reduce item switching.
litematica-printer.config.printSkipShulk: Skip shulker box blocks entirely while printing.

litematica-printer.config.printShulkerAf: Place ordinary blocks first when other pending targets are nearby.
litematica-printer.config.printBreakWron: Allow breaking and re-placing blocks whose type matches but state does not.
litematica-printer.config.printFillCauld: Fill empty cauldrons with water, lava or powder snow using buckets.
litematica-printer.config.printFastDirec: Extend the work area along the movement direction when moving fast.
litematica-printer.config.printerAutoEna: Turn the work switch on automatically when a schematic is loaded.
litematica-printer.config.placeDefaultDi: Preferred face when several are valid.
litematica-printer.config.handRestockShu: Automatically refill the consumed item from a shulker box back into its original slot (requires Quick Shulker).

Blocks rendered when the option above is on.
litematica-printer.config.printScanWhite: When on, printing only handles blocks in the whitelist; an empty list means no restriction.
Blocks allowed by the print scan whitelist; item IDs, Chinese names and # tags are supported.
